title: Quantum Mpemba Speedups in the Thermodynamics of Landauer Erasure
abstract: We investigate how nonequilibrium quantum initial states can reduce the finite-time thermodynamic cost of Landauer erasure. Considering a general finite-dimensional quantum memory coupled to a thermal reservoir via a Davies generator, we show that the dissipated heat at a fixed operational erasure fidelity is largely controlled by the overlap of the initial state with the slowest Liouvillian relaxation mode. We derive a modified finite-time Landauer bound in which the excess dissipation above the quasistatic limit scales quadratically with this slow mode projection, and we prove a sufficient Mpemba Landauer condition under which a hotter state can erase faster and dissipate less heat than a colder preparation, without violating Landauer's principle. A minimal qutrit model illustrates these quantum Mpemba speedups and reveals broad parameter regimes where coherence and Hamiltonian-induced modes conspire to suppress finite-time entropy production. We further identify practical control knobs, including temperature tuning, coherence engineering, and Hamiltonian shaping of Liouvillian spectra, which enable Mpemba-enhanced erasure to be directly tested on platforms such as superconducting circuits, trapped ions, semiconductor quantum dots, and solid-state spins.
summary: The paper explores how preparing a quantum memory in a non-equilibrium, hot state can accelerate the erasure process and reduce the minimum heat dissipated compared to standard cold preparations. It achieves this by leveraging the spectral properties of the system's Liouvillian evolution, establishing a quantifiable 'Mpemba–Landauer condition' for such speedups.
main_problem: The research investigates how non-equilibrium quantum initial states can reduce the finite-time thermodynamic cost associated with Landauer erasure.
main_result: A modified Landauer bound is derived showing excess dissipation scales quadratically with the slow mode projection, and a 'Mpemba–Landauer condition' proves that hotter states can erase faster and dissipate less heat than colder ones without violating Landauer's principle.
method: The analysis utilizes Liouvillian spectral theory to decompose time evolution into relaxation modes, focusing on the single slowest mode approximation for thermodynamic cost calculations.
model_or_system: The system is a general finite-dimensional quantum memory coupled to a thermal reservoir via a Davies generator. Illustrations use a minimal qutrit model, and practical applications are suggested for superconducting circuits or trapped ions.
key_observables: Dissipated heat into the bath (Q_bath), operational erasure time ($	au_{erase}$), and the overlap coefficients ($c_j$) quantifying initial state relaxation modes.
important_parameters: Preparation temperature ($T_{prep}$), fidelity target ($p_{target}$), and the spectral gap defined by the slowest Liouvillian eigenvalue ($\lambda_1$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on controlled approximations, specifically assuming that higher-order Liouvillian modes decay much faster than the single slowest mode.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the general setup of Mpemba-enhanced erasure, showing population dynamics ($p_0(t)$) for hot vs. cold preparations, and plotting $	au_{erase}$ and $Q_{bath}(	au_{erase})$ versus preparation temperature to confirm speedup/cooling effects.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the general Liouvillian framework (eigenmodes, spectral decomposition), deriving the modified Landauer bound using slow-mode approximations, proving the Mpemba–Landauer condition via comparison of hot vs. cold protocols, and concluding with practical control knobs for implementation.
why_interesting: This work directly connects non-equilibrium thermodynamics (Mpemba effect) to fundamental quantum information processing limits (Landauer principle), providing concrete physical mechanisms for improving computational efficiency in open quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. A general setup of quantum Mpemba–enhanced Landauer erasure. A quantum memory is encoded in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space with logical-zero subspace, and logical-one is stored in the orthogonal complement. The system is initially prepared in a thermal state ρth(Tprep) of an input Hamiltonian, then quenched to an erasure Hamiltonian and weakly coupled to a bath at temperature Tb, generating Lindblad dynamics that drive the memory toward the logical zero subspace.

FIG. 2. Finite-time Landauer cost and Mpemba advantage in a qutrit memory. Erasure dynamics for a minimal three-level model coupled to a thermal bath at temperature Tb = 0.6. The population p0(t) of the logical-zero level is shown for two thermal preparations at different temperatures T (c) prep (cold in blue solid line) and T (h) prep > T (c) prep (hot in orange dashed line), evolving under the same Davies generator. The hotter preparation reaches the target fidelity ptarget at a shorter erasure time τ(h) erase < τ(c) erase, while the accumulated dissipated heat at erasure satisfies Q(h) bath(τ(h) erase) < Q(c) bath(τ(c) erase), thereby realizing a genuine quantum Mpemba–enhanced Landauer...

FIG. 3. Erasure time and finite-time thermodynamic cost as a function of the preparation temperature in the qutrit memory of Fig. 2. Left: operational erasure time τerase versus Tprep for bath temperature Tb = 0.6 and erasure Hamiltonian. Right: total dissipated heat at erasure Qbath(τerase), with the dotted line indicating the quasistatic LB kBTb ln 2. Both quantities show a strong dependence on Tprep and exhibit broad parameter regimes in which hotter preparations simultaneously reduce τerase and Qbath, realizing Mpemba–enhanced Landauer erasure for many hot–cold pairs. The Hamiltonian parameters are the same as Fig. 2.
